# M5 gate (a): spoken form of every equation segment and inline-maths sentence, convention spec 3c
one is two standard deviations less than the mean of five because: 1 equals 5 plus minus 2 times 2.
the equation value equals mean plus number of stdevs times standard deviation can be expressed for a sample and for a population.
sample: x equals x bar plus number of stdev times s
population: x equals mu plus number of stdev times sigma
the lower case letter s represents the sample standard deviation and the greek letter sigma sigma, lower case represents the population standard deviation.
the symbol x bar is the sample mean and the greek symbol mu is the population mean.
if x is a number, then the difference x minus mean is called its deviation.
if the numbers belong to a population, in symbols a deviation is x minus mu.
for sample data, in symbols a deviation is x minus x bar.
the lower case letter s represents the sample standard deviation and the greek letter sigma sigma, lower case represents the population standard deviation.
if the sample has the same characteristics as the population, then s should be a good estimate of sigma.
the variance is the average of the squares of the deviations the x minus x bar values for a sample, or the x minus mu values for a population.
the symbol sigma squared represents the population variance; the population standard deviation sigma is the square root of the population variance.
the symbol s squared represents the sample variance; the sample standard deviation s is the square root of the sample variance.
if the numbers come from a census of the entire population and not a sample, when we calculate the average of the squared deviations to find the variance, we divide by n, the number of items in the population.
if the data are from a sample rather than a population, when we calculate the average of the squared deviations, we divide by n minus 1, one less than the number of items in the sample.
s equals the square root of the fraction the sum of x minus x bar squared over n minus 1, end fraction or s equals the square root of the fraction the sum of f times x minus x bar squared over n minus 1, end fraction
for the sample standard deviation, the denominator is n minus 1, that is the sample size minus 1.
sigma equals the square root of the fraction the sum of x minus mu squared over n, end fraction or sigma equals the square root of the fraction the sum of f times x minus mu squared over n, end fraction
for the population standard deviation, the denominator is n, the number of items in the population.
in these formulas, f represents the frequency with which a value appears.
for example, if a value appears once, f is one.
if a value appears three times in the data set or population, f is three.
the notation for the standard error of the mean is sigma over the square root of n where sigma is the standard deviation of the population and n is the size of the sample.
